effect: The outer layer reduced water loss, making the remaining skin support and sensory parts the next priorities.

reason: The supporting layer and surface barrier appear to be complementary layers of skin.

effect: The final result shows how touch signals and muscle activity work together to steady the glass, completing the chapter.
reaction: The slipping-glass sequence gives the earlier construction a clear purpose.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was the most worthwhile action: it brought protection, sensation, control and muscle work together in an everyday situation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the supporting layer to the surface barrier felt more like assembly than a decision, though the resulting cross-section helped show where the vessels lie.

surprise.text: I found it useful that the skin's outer layer slows water loss without being completely waterproof, while living cells beneath replace its dead cells.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary. The item descriptions and successive goals gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would be interested in another chapter if it offered another concrete situation like the slipping glass. The connections between body systems held my interest more than the straightforward layer assembly.
